claims.text: The unmodified (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy has a large caloric response.
The unmodified alloy has poor load-bearing integrity and tends to crack under load.
Adding approximately 1 at% Nb will produce nanoscale Nb-rich precipitates.
Adding approximately 1 at% Nb will refine the alloy's grain-boundary structure.
Nb-rich precipitates and refined grain boundaries will obstruct or deflect crack propagation.
Obstructing or deflecting crack propagation will increase ductility and fracture toughness.
At approximately 1 at% Nb, the primary structural transition responsible for the caloric effect will remain largely unaffected.
At approximately 1 at% Nb, the primary magnetostructural transition responsible for the caloric effect will remain largely unaffected.
The Nb-modified alloy will have greater fracture toughness and resistance to cracking than the unmodified alloy.
The Nb-modified alloy's fracture toughness or ductility will improve by at least 10% relative to the unmodified alloy.
The Nb-modified alloy's isothermal entropy change or adiabatic temperature change will remain within 10% of that of the unmodified alloy.
The proposed integrity and caloric outcomes apply at magnetic fields up to approximately 2 T.
The proposed integrity and caloric outcomes apply at pressures up to approximately 100 MPa.
The proposed integrity and caloric outcomes apply over approximately 250–400 K near the caloric transformation.
The proposed integrity improvement applies under mechanical loads near the unmodified alloy's failure threshold.
Nb additions much higher than approximately 1 at% may disrupt the caloric transition.
Prior preliminary evidence supports grain-boundary strengthening through minor Nb additions.
Processing-route and microstructural variability may alter the degree of integrity improvement and caloric preservation.
